overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole met to review proposed fiscal year 2023 department budgets for assessing, health, treasury, community media, historical preservation, parking enforcement, and veterans services. No final budget votes were taken during the meeting.

items.title: Assessor Department Budget
items.summary: Interim Chief Assessor Ellen Brideau presented the proposed Assessor budget, detailing personnel updates, technology efficiencies, and reductions in professional services and legal lines.

items.title: Board of Health and Animal Control Budgets
items.summary: Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor reviewed the Health Department and Animal Control budgets, addressing grant-funded positions, upcoming rodent control initiatives, and lab biosafety regulations.

items.title: Treasury and Collector Department Budget
items.summary: Treasurer Collector Judy Johnston presented the department budget, highlighting salary reductions due to staff turnover and increased funding for tax title collections.

items.title: Civil Defense Budget
items.summary: Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor briefly presented the Civil Defense budget, which experienced no changes from the prior fiscal year.

items.title: Medford Community Media Budget
items.summary: Station Manager Kevin Harrington presented the local access budget, discussing minor salary adjustments and planned equipment replacements.

items.title: Historical Commission Budget
items.summary: Council President Nicole Morell read a statement from Historical Commission Chair Jennifer Keenan requesting matching grant funds, prompting council discussion regarding the city's demolition delay ordinance.

items.title: Parking Enforcement Budget
items.summary: Parking Director Faye Morrison and Finance Director Bob Dickinson discussed the parking enforcement budget and answered council questions on department staffing and early revenue figures.

items.title: Veterans Services Budget
items.summary: Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian presented the Veterans Services budget and announced the appointment of Jeremy Johns as the city's new Veterans Services Director.
